newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian military talks peace with Khmer Rouge.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian military talks peace with Khmer Rouge.

text.p: A senior Cambodian army official said on Wednesday that top military personnel recently traveled to Thailand's border with Cambodia to urge remaining Khmer Rouge hardliners to stop fighting and join the government.
"We have met with a go-between a few days ago at the border, but we have not yet heard a response from the hardliners," said the official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.
The Maoist guerrillas have been decimated in recent months by waves of defections. Only between 800 and 2,000 Khmer Rouge hardliners are thought to remain.
Military officials and analysts said the rebels are concentrated at Anlong Veng, the hardliners' northwest base near the Thai border.
The Khmer Rouge, which led Cambodia during the genocidal 1975-1979 "Killing Fields" era, have continued to sound defiant notes via clandestine radio broacasts.
In a broadcast monitored in Phnom Penh on Wednesday, rebels warned the Cambodian government that soldiers would die if it persisted in reopening a highway near rebel-held territory.

Route 12, which runs from the central province of Kompong Thom to that of Preah Vihear in the north, has historically been a flashpoint between government troops and the Maoist guerrillas, said military analysts.
Rebels have continued to carry out isolated attacks in recent days as the government seeks to reopen the road.

Khmer Rouge nominal leader Khieu Samphan, also speaking on Wednesday's guerrilla radio broadcast, condemned a government plan to rehabilitate Route 10, which accesses former rebel bases in the northwest, with U.S. funding.
The Khmer Rouge joined three other parties in signing a U.N.-sponsored peace pact for Cambodia in 1991, but later reneged on the deal and have been fighting the coalition government elected in 1993.
More than a million Cambodians were either murdered as suspected enemies or died from overwork or lack of health care during the Khmer Rouge's reign.
